docs.title: netbox-more-metrics
docs.text: Create custom metrics and export information from NetBox into your timeseries database.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: NetBox Version Plugin Version 3.4 <= 3.7 0.1.X, 0.2.X 4.0 <= 4.5 0.3.X, 0.4.X 4.0 <= 4.7 0.5.X

docs.title: Installing
docs.text: For adding to a NetBox Docker setup see the general instructions for using netbox-docker with plugins.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install netbox-more-metrics

or by adding to your local_requirements.txt or plugin_requirements.txt (netbox-docker):

netbox-more-metrics

docs.title: Development Install
docs.text:
If you would like to install a version not yet published to pypi.

pip install git+https://github.com/TheDJVG/netbox-more-metrics

or by adding to your local_requirements.txt or plugin_requirements.txt (netbox-docker):

git+https://github.com/TheDJVG/netbox-more-metrics

docs.title: NetBox Configuration
docs.text:
Enable the plugin in /opt/netbox/netbox/netbox/configuration.py, or if you use netbox-docker, your /configuration/plugins.py file :

PLUGINS = [
    'netbox_more_metrics'
]

If you want to export the configured metrics without authentication set the plugin config export_metrics_without_auth to True. By default, normal NetBox view permissions apply. 

PLUGINS_CONFIG = {
    'netbox_more_metrics' : {
        'export_metrics_without_auth': True
    }
}

docs.title: Custom metrics
docs.text:
For example, you could track the amount of active devices over time by rack and site:

  • Export Gauge, Counter, and Info Prometheus metrics from NetBox models (DCIM, IPAM, Circuits, Virtualization, Tenancy, etc.).
  • Group data by one or more model fields (metric_labels), including relational fields (site__slug, rack__name) and custom fields (custom_field_data__my_field), and rename exported labels cleanly via label_renames.
  • Export either aggregated object counts (count) or built-in utilization percentages:
  • dcim.Rack: Space utilization (get_utilization) and power utilization (get_power_utilization)
  • ipam.Prefix: IP utilization (get_utilization)
  • ipam.Aggregate: Prefix utilization (get_utilization)
  • Filter and exclude source querysets with Django ORM JSON dictionaries (filter and exclude).
  • Full NetBox 4.x integration including UI & REST API FilterSets, global search indexing, tags, custom fields, changelogs, and journals.

docs.title: Filter & security validation
docs.text:
Every filter, exclude rule, and label path is validated on save and when collectors initialize:

Sensitive authentication/credential models (such as users and auth) and ReDoS-prone regex lookups are automatically blocked from metric queries and relation traversals.

docs.title: Heavy lifting is done by the database
docs.text: As much as possible is aggregated directly in PostgreSQL to take advantage of model indexes and database optimizations. NULL database values are exported as the string "null".

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
• Global endpoint: Collections with include_in_default=True are automatically registered in NetBox's global /metrics endpoint (when METRICS_ENABLED=True).
  • Per-collection & per-metric endpoints: Enabled MetricCollections (/plugins/more-metrics/collections/<id>/metrics/) and Metrics (/plugins/more-metrics/metrics/<id>/metrics/) can be scraped individually.

docs.title: Development & Testing
docs.text:
Start the local NetBox development environment with Docker Compose:

make start

Run the automated test suite inside the NetBox container:

docker compose run --rm -e DEBUG=False netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics

To build and test against a specific NetBox 4.x version (e.g. v4.2 or v4.7):

NETBOX_VER=v4.7 docker compose build --build-arg NETBOX_VER=v4.7 netbox
NETBOX_VER=v4.7 docker compose run --rm -e DEBUG=False netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics

See docs/netbox_upgrade_strategy.md for details on CI matrix testing and maintaining compatibility with future NetBox releases.

docs.title: Long-Term NetBox Upgrade and Maintenance Strategy Guide
docs.text: This document establishes the official long-term upgrade, compatibility maintenance, and operational lifecycle strategy for the netbox-more-metrics plugin. It is designed as an exhaustive, production-grade guide for maintainers, contributors, and enterprise site reliability engineers managing custom Prometheus metric exports across NetBox minor (4.0 → 4.1 → 4.2 → ...) and major (4.x → 5.x) version transitions.

docs.title: 1.1 Purpose and Scope
docs.text:
The netbox-more-metrics plugin bridges the NetBox Network Source of Truth (NSoT) with Prometheus monitoring infrastructure by exposing dynamic database queries as standardized Prometheus exposition metrics. Because the plugin interfaces directly with NetBox internal data models, Django ORM internals, NetBox plugin lifecycle hooks, and Prometheus exposition registries, upstream changes in NetBox core, Django, or Python runtime environments have direct architectural implications.

This guide provides the protocols, checklists, and technical patterns necessary to guarantee seamless upgrades, eliminate backward-compatibility breaks, and ensure continuous automated testing at zero infrastructure cost.

docs.title: 1.2 Guiding Engineering Principles
docs.text:
All maintenance, feature development, and upstream upgrades must adhere strictly to four core engineering tenets:

  1. Zero Infrastructure Cost: Continuous integration and validation workflows must execute entirely on free GitHub-hosted runners (ubuntu-latest) using open-source service containers and native caching. No paid build runners, third-party SaaS CI tiers, or proprietary hosting services are permitted.
  2. Zero Prometheus Scrape Disruption (Fail-Soft Isolation): A single misconfigured metric, database query error, or transient upstream model change must never cause an unhandled HTTP 500 error on /plugins/more-metrics/export/ or /metrics. Scrapes must fail-soft: capture exceptions, log diagnostic warnings, and yield healthy metric families without crashing Prometheus scrapers or triggering false-positive alerts.
  3. Zero Unannounced Breakages (Proactive Cadence Tracking): Maintainers must never discover upstream incompatibilities from end-user failure reports. Weekly automated canary pipelines and pre-release testing against NetBox release candidates provide a 3-to-4 week remediation window before upstream general availability (GA).
  4. Strict Architectural Adherence: Never introduce monkey-patches, bypass Django migration graphs, or violate NetBox plugin extension patterns. Always leverage official NetBox APIs (NetBoxModel, NetBoxModelFilterSet, SearchIndex, ObjectType, PluginConfig).

docs.title: 1.3 NetBox & Dependency Version Support Matrix
docs.text: Component Minimum Supported Active / Tested Target Future / Planned Target Deprecated / Unsupported NetBox Core 4.0.0 4.0.x, 4.1.x, 4.2.x, 4.5.x 4.6+, 5.0.x NetBox < 3.4 (Dropped) Python Runtime 3.10 (for NetBox 4.0–4.2) 3.11, 3.12 3.13 (upon NetBox adoption) Python < 3.10 (Dropped) Django Framework 5.0 5.0.x, 5.1.x 5.2 LTS, 6.0 Django < 4.2 (Dropped) PostgreSQL Database 14.0 15.x, 16.x, 18-alpine (dev) 17.x+ PostgreSQL < 14 Redis / Valkey 7.0 7.x, 8.x 8.x+ Redis < 7.0 prometheus-client 0.20.0 0.20.0+ 0.21+ / OpenMetrics 1.0 prometheus-client < 0.14

docs.title: 2.1 Upstream Release Lifecycle & Deprecation Policy
docs.text: Upstream NetBox follows Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) aligned with a predictable release schedule: - Patch Releases (4.x.Y): Released weekly to bi-weekly. Contain bug fixes, security remediations, and performance adjustments. Patch releases strictly preserve backward compatibility for database schemas, models, and public plugin APIs. - Minor Releases (4.X.0): Released approximately every four months (typically April, August, and December). Minor releases introduce new features, model changes, and UI improvements. - The "2-Minor Deprecation Rule": Upstream NetBox policy dictates that when a core API or pattern is slated for deprecation, it emits DeprecationWarning or PendingDeprecationWarning for at least two minor releases before removal. For instance, a feature deprecated in NetBox 4.1 remains functional with warnings in 4.1 and 4.2, and is only removed in 4.3 or 5.0. - Major Releases (X.0.0): Released every 18 to 24 months. Major releases mark significant architectural evolutions (e.g., dropping legacy Django versions, transitioning core model inheritance, or overhauling UI frameworks).

docs.title: 2.2 Monitoring Channels & Feeds
docs.text: Maintainers must track upcoming changes across four primary upstream channels: 1. GitHub Releases Feed: Subscribe to https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/releases.atom via RSS or GitHub Notifications ("Custom → Releases"). 2. Upstream Release Notes: Consult https://netboxlabs.com/docs/netbox/en/stable/release-notes/ prior to every minor release upgrade. 3. GitHub Discussions (Feature Requests & Architecture): Monitor https://github.com/netbox-community/netbox/discussions/categories/announcements for early notice on major architectural shifts. 4. Upstream Commit Stream on develop: Periodically review commits targeting netbox-community/netbox:develop to identify database schema modifications and deprecations months before release.

docs.title: 2.3 Automated Upstream Canary Workflow
docs.text:
To eliminate manual monitoring overhead, an automated canary workflow runs weekly on GitHub Actions. It queries the GitHub REST API for the latest NetBox release tag, verifies whether the tag is currently tested in the CI matrix, and opens an issue if a new minor release is detected.

The workflow definition (.github/workflows/canary.yml or integrated cron) runs at zero cost on ubuntu-latest:

---
name: Upstream NetBox Release Canary

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1' # Every Monday at 06:00 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: upstream-canary
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check-upstream:
    name: Check Upstream NetBox Releases
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Fetch Latest NetBox Release
        id: get_release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          LATEST_TAG=$(gh api repos/netbox-community/netbox/releases/latest --jq .tag_name)
          echo "latest_tag=${LATEST_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Latest upstream NetBox release is: ${LATEST_TAG}"

      - name: Check Against Active Support Matrix
        id: verify_matrix
        run: |
          LATEST="${{ steps.get_release.outputs.latest_tag }}"
          # Extract major.minor (e.g. v4.5)
          MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | grep -oE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')
          echo "Upstream minor branch: ${MINOR}"
          # Read supported versions from repository configuration
          SUPPORTED="v4.0 v4.1 v4.2 v4.5"
          if [[ ! " ${SUPPORTED} " =~ " ${MINOR} " ]]; then
            echo "new_minor_detected=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "new_minor_detected=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Open Issue for New Upstream Minor Release
        if: steps.verify_matrix.outputs.new_minor_detected == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          TAG="${{ steps.get_release.outputs.latest_tag }}"
          gh issue create \
            --title "Upstream Compatibility: New NetBox Minor Release ${TAG}" \
            --body "A new upstream NetBox release **${TAG}** has been published. Maintainers must execute the Minor Upgrade Playbook to update the CI matrix and certify plugin compatibility."

docs.title: 2.4 Pre-Release Testing Protocol
docs.text:
Before each NetBox minor release (e.g., 4.3.0), the NetBox core team publishes Beta and Release Candidate (RC) builds (e.g., v4.3.0-beta1, v4.3.0-rc1): 1. Lead Time: Beta/RC builds appear 3 to 4 weeks prior to general availability. 2. Local RC Verification: Maintainers test the RC container image locally: 

NETBOX_VER=v4.3.0-rc1 docker compose build netbox
NETBOX_VER=v4.3.0-rc1 docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py makemigrations --check
NETBOX_VER=v4.3.0-rc1 docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics --keepdb
3. Deprecation Trapping: Run test executions with warning escalation to capture upcoming breaks: 
docker compose run --rm netbox python -W error::DeprecationWarning ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics --keepdb

docs.title: 3.1 Django Upgrade Cycles
docs.text: NetBox tracks modern Django LTS and stable branches. NetBox 4.x runs on Django 5.x; NetBox 5.0 is slated to adopt Django 5.2 LTS or Django 6.0: - django.utils.timezone: Avoid deprecated naive datetime comparisons; always use timezone.now() and timezone-aware timestamps for collector scheduling and metric timestamps. - QuerySet Semantics: Django 5.0+ introduces stricter rules for annotation aliases and grouping. Avoid raw extra() or direct SQL fragment injection. - Escalation Testing: CI test runs should periodically execute with PYTHONWARNINGS="error::DeprecationWarning" to pinpoint APIs scheduled for removal in future Django releases.

docs.title: 3.2 NetBox Core Model & ObjectType Abstractions
docs.text:
NetBox 4.0 replaced Django's generic django.contrib.contenttypes.models.ContentType with core.models.ObjectType: - Model References: Metric.content_type points to core.ObjectType. All dynamic queries querying available object types must filter via ObjectType.objects.public() or exclude sensitive apps: 

SENSITIVE_APP_LABELS = {
    "users",
    "auth",
    "contenttypes",
    "sessions",
    "admin",
}
- Relational Field Path Traversal: In netbox_more_metrics/models.py, validate_field_path() traverses relational lookups using Django _meta.get_field(). When NetBox renames models or replaces relations (e.g., converting foreign keys to generic relations), maintainers must verify that _meta.get_field(part).related_model correctly resolves the destination model without leaking private attributes or throwing unhandled FieldDoesNotExist exceptions.

docs.title: 3.3 NetBox Plugin Framework Evolution
docs.text:
The plugin configuration class (netbox_more_metrics/__init__.py:NetBoxMoreMetricsConfig) defines the plugin's operational boundaries: 

class NetBoxMoreMetricsConfig(PluginConfig):
    name = "netbox_more_metrics"
    verbose_name = "More Metrics"
    description = "Export custom metrics from NetBox data."
    version = "0.4.1"
    min_version = "4.0.0"
    max_version = "4.99.9"
    author = "Daan van Gorkum"
    author_email = "me+netbox@dj.vg"
    base_url = "more-metrics"
    default_settings = {
        "export_metrics_without_auth": False,
    }
- min_version: Set to "4.0.0". Never lower this below 4.0 because legacy NetBox 3.x support has been completely dropped. - max_version: Pin to "4.99.9". This prevents end-users from installing the plugin on uncertified NetBox 5.x major versions where breaking core changes could cause system instability. - ready() Lifecycle: Keep ready() fast and non-blocking. Database queries in ready() must be wrapped in try/except (OperationalError, ProgrammingError) to ensure management commands like migrate or collectstatic can execute during initial database provisioning.

docs.title: 3.4 NetBox FilterSets, SearchIndex, and Tables Modernization
docs.text:
• FilterSet Standards: Subclass netbox.filtersets.NetBoxModelFilterSet. Ensure all custom models (MetricCollection, Metric) implement filter parameters for standard attributes (q, name, enabled, tags).
  • SearchIndex Standards: Register all user-facing models using netbox.search.SearchIndex and register_search(). Assign weighted relevance (1000 for primary identifiers like name, 2000 for metric identifiers like metric_name).
  • Table Classes: Subclass netbox.tables.NetBoxTable. Ensure table actions, column selections, and tag badges utilize standard NetBox UI components.

docs.title: 3.5 Django REST Framework (DRF) & API Serializer Compatibility
docs.text:
• Model Serializers: Subclass netbox.api.serializers.NetBoxModelSerializer.
  • Mandatory Audit Fields: Always include standard audit attributes: id, url, display, name, description, tags, custom_fields, created, last_updated.
  • Brief Serializers: Subclass netbox.api.serializers.NestedGroupModelSerializer or WritableNestedSerializer providing lightweight representations (id, url, display, name) for nested relational serialization.
  • Authentication & ViewSet Permissions: Ensure all viewsets enforce NetBoxModelViewSet permission classes. Never set permission_classes = [] on operational endpoints.

docs.title: 3.6 UI Templates & Frontend Asset Evolution
docs.text:
• Template Inheritance: Extend official NetBox templates:
  • Detail views: {% extends 'generic/object.html' %}
  • List views: {% extends 'generic/object_list.html' %}
  • Edit/Create views: {% extends 'generic/object_edit.html' %}
  • HTMX & Bootstrap 5: NetBox 4.x utilizes Bootstrap 5 and HTMX. Avoid bundling separate heavy JavaScript dependencies (e.g., jQuery, Vue, React). Use native HTML5 data attributes and NetBox CSS helper classes.

docs.title: 4.1 Database Migration Hygiene & CI Validation
docs.text:
Database migrations are the most critical aspect of plugin upgrade safety. An unmigrated model modification or invalid migration dependency can prevent NetBox from starting or corrupt production database schemas. - Strict Migration Immutability: Once a migration file (e.g., 0001 through 0008) is merged into the default branch or published in a release, it is permanently immutable. Never alter, re-generate, or delete existing migration files. - Mandatory CI Gate: Every CI build executes: 

docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py makemigrations --check
This command fails with a non-zero exit code if any model change was made without generating a matching migration file.

docs.title: 4.2 The "Leaf Migration Dependency" Pitfall & Manual Dependency Pinning
docs.text:
CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL WARNING: THE LEAF-MIGRATION DEPENDENCY TRAP

When developers execute ./manage.py makemigrations netbox_more_metrics inside a modern development environment (e.g., NetBox 4.5), Django inspects all foreign keys pointing to external apps (such as core.ObjectType). By default, Django automatically sets the dependency of the new migration to the current leaf migration of the target app.

In NetBox 4.5, the leaf migration for core is 0021_job_queue_name.

If the newly generated plugin migration contains: 

dependencies = [
    ('core', '0021_job_queue_name'),
    ('netbox_more_metrics', '0007_metric_exclude'),
]
Then any user running NetBox 4.0, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, or 4.4 who upgrades or installs the plugin will experience an immediate crash during python manage.py migrate: 
django.db.migrations.exceptions.NodeNotFoundError: Migration netbox_more_metrics.0008_...
dependencies reference nonexistent parent node ('core', '0021_job_queue_name')
Because core.0021 does not exist in earlier NetBox 4.x releases, the entire upgrade aborts.

docs.title: Remediation Protocol: Manual Dependency Pinning
docs.text:
Whenever makemigrations creates a new migration file: 1. Open the generated file in netbox_more_metrics/migrations/. 2. Inspect the dependencies list. 3. Identify dependencies on upstream NetBox core apps (core, dcim, ipam, extras). 4. Pin the dependency to the earliest migration that introduced the required model or field, rather than the latest leaf migration. - For core.ObjectType, model proxying was introduced in ('core', '0008_contenttype_proxy') and stabilized in ('core', '0010_gfk_indexes') or ('core', '0018_concrete_objecttype'). - Update the dependency to reference the lowest common denominator present across all supported versions (v4.0+): 

dependencies = [
    ('core', '0008_contenttype_proxy'),
    ('netbox_more_metrics', '0007_metric_exclude'),
]
5. Test the migration across the CI version matrix (v4.0, v4.1, v4.2, v4.5) to verify that all versions can resolve the migration dependency graph.

docs.title: 4.3 Safe Schema Evolution & Preserving User Configurations
docs.text: When introducing new fields or database schema changes to Metric or MetricCollection: 1. Always Provide Defaults or Allow Nulls: - New boolean fields: default=False or default=True with db_index=True if queried frequently. - New relational fields: null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL. - New JSON/Array fields: default=dict or default=list with blank=True. 2. Never Rename Columns in a Single Destructive Step: Renaming a database column directly causes immediate downtime for active scrapers during rolling NetBox container upgrades. Use multi-phase field deprecation.

docs.title: 4.4 Multi-Phase Field Deprecation & Data Migrations
docs.text:
When removing or transforming database fields: - Phase 1 (Release N): Add the new column with null=True. Update models and collectors to read from the new field if populated, falling back to the legacy field. - Phase 2 (Release N): Include a Python data migration (RunPython) that iterates over existing records and copies data from the legacy field to the new field: 

def forward_copy_data(apps, schema_editor):
    Metric = apps.get_model('netbox_more_metrics', 'Metric')
    for metric in Metric.objects.all():
        if metric.legacy_field and not metric.new_field:
            metric.new_field = transform(metric.legacy_field)
            metric.save(update_fields=['new_field'])

class Migration(migrations.Migration):
    operations = [
        migrations.RunPython(forward_copy_data, reverse_code=migrations.RunPython.noop),
    ]
- Phase 3 (Release N+1): Emit deprecation warnings in UI forms and API serializers if the legacy field is supplied. - Phase 4 (Release N+2 or Major Bump): Remove the legacy field from models and generate the final schema drop migration.

docs.title: 4.5 Migration Reversibility Testing & PostgreSQL Specifics
docs.text:
• Reversibility Testing: Maintainers must verify that all schema migrations can be unapplied cleanly without data loss or integrity violations: 
    # Step backwards one migration
docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py migrate netbox_more_metrics 0007
# Re-apply forward
docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py migrate netbox_more_metrics
  • PostgreSQL Concurrency Considerations:
  • Adding non-null columns without defaults in PostgreSQL locks the entire table.
  • Adding indexes on large tables in production should use ConcurrentAddIndex if supported, or keep index footprint minimal.

docs.title: 5. Dynamic Collector Compatibility & Prometheus Exposition Stability
5.1 Dynamic Collector Architecture Overview & Scrape Flow
docs.text: The plugin operates an in-memory dynamic collector architecture: 1. An incoming HTTP request hits /plugins/more-metrics/export/ or a specific collection/metric endpoint. 2. The view authenticates the request or verifies export_metrics_without_auth == True. 3. DynamicMetricCollectionCollector instantiates or retrieves the collection's active metrics. 4. Each metric is evaluated by DynamicMetricCollector, which translates model selections, filters, exclusions, and relational lookups into an optimized Django ORM QuerySet. 5. The QuerySet executes against PostgreSQL, extracting counts, values, or utilization percentages. 6. The collector constructs Prometheus metric families (GaugeMetricFamily, CounterMetricFamily, InfoMetricFamily) and serializes them to exposition format.

docs.title: 5.2 Upstream Model & Method Changes
docs.text:
Dynamic collectors frequently evaluate model methods (e.g., get_utilization, get_power_utilization): - Defensive Evaluation: NetBox model methods may change signatures, return None, or be deprecated. The evaluation loop in netbox_more_metrics/collectors.py must guard method invocations defensively: 

try:
    raw_val = getattr(result, self.metric_value)
    value = raw_val() if callable(raw_val) else raw_val
    if value is None:
        continue
except (AttributeError, TypeError, Exception) as exc:
    logger.warning("Failed evaluating metric value '%s' on %r: %s", self.metric_value, result, exc)
    continue
- ORM Traversal Hardening: Relational paths (device__rack__site__name) must be validated against validate_field_path() to ensure that intermediate models cannot traverse into sensitive objects (User, Token, Session).

docs.title: 5.3 Fail-Soft Error Isolation
docs.text: Under no circumstances should an error in one metric abort the scrape of all other metrics. If an admin configures an invalid filter or an upstream NetBox model alters an attribute: 1. Catch exceptions within DynamicMetricCollector.collect(). 2. Emit a structured log message (logger.error("Error collecting metric %s (pk=%d): %s", self.metric_name, self.pk, exc, exc_info=True)). 3. Do not re-raise the exception to the top-level view. 4. Allow all remaining metrics in the collection to complete and yield valid Prometheus metrics. 5. This guarantees that Prometheus scrapers receive HTTP 200 with all healthy metrics, preventing scrape alert storms across production network monitoring infrastructure.

docs.title: 5.4 Relational Label Sanitization & PostgreSQL JSON Extraction
docs.text:
• Label Sanitization (get_annotation_alias): Django ORM forbids double underscores in annotation aliases (e.g., device__site__name is invalid as an alias). The plugin transforms relational label paths into safe PostgreSQL aliases (_metric_label_device_site_name) with collision-resistant SHA-256 truncation.
  • PostgreSQL JSONB Custom Fields: NetBox custom fields are stored in custom_field_data JSONB columns. Dynamic collectors use jsonb_extract_path_text to extract values directly in the database engine, avoiding costly Python deserialization loops. Maintain compatibility with PostgreSQL JSONB query semantics across PostgreSQL 14, 15, and 16.

docs.title: 5.5 Prometheus Client Library Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Registry Suffix Collision Prevention: prometheus_client automatically strips _total from Counters and _info from Info metrics in its internal name map (_names_to_collectors). Previous plugin versions crashed when querying self.registry._names_to_collectors because checking metric.metric_name resulted in false-negative existence checks, triggering duplicate registration errors.
  • Explicit Collector Tracking: The plugin explicitly manages active collectors via an internal dictionary keyed by primary key: 
    self._active_metric_collectors: dict[int, DynamicMetricCollector] = {}
    This eliminates duplicate collector registration crashes regardless of suffix naming (_total, _info, _count, _bucket).
  • OpenMetrics Compliance: Ensure exposition conforms to Prometheus text format 0.0.4 and OpenMetrics 1.0 specifications.

docs.title: 6. Zero-Cost GitHub Actions CI/CD Maintenance Strategy
6.1 GitHub-Hosted Runner Economics
docs.text:
Public open-source repositories on GitHub receive unlimited free runner minutes on standard GitHub-hosted runners (ubuntu-latest). Private repositories receive 2,000 free minutes per month.

To ensure long-term maintenance costs remain $0.00: - Concurrency Auto-Cancellation: Every workflow includes a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true: 

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
When a developer pushes multiple commits in quick succession, previous in-flight runs are immediately terminated, preserving runner capacity. - Aggressive Timeouts: All jobs specify timeout-minutes: 10 (or 15 for matrix tests) to ensure hung processes or stalled container pulls cannot consume hours of runner time. - Execution Efficiency: With Docker Compose and caching, a full test run of 231 tests completes in under 20 seconds. Total pipeline wall-clock time across the 4-version NetBox matrix is under 2.5 minutes.

docs.title: 6.2 Native Service Container Architecture
docs.text: The CI architecture leverages Docker Compose running directly on the ubuntu-latest host. This guarantees: 1. Complete parity with local development environments (compose.yaml). 2. Immediate availability of official pre-built netboxcommunity/netbox images without requiring developers to clone NetBox core and compile 50+ Python dependencies from scratch. 3. Isolated database and caching services using official alpine containers (postgres:18-alpine, redis:8-alpine).

docs.title: 6.3 Aggressive Multi-Tier Caching
docs.text:
• Docker Layer Caching: GitHub Actions runner SSDs cache container layers and intermediate build stages.
  • Python Package Caching: The fast packaging-and-quality job uses actions/setup-python@v5 with cache: "pip" to cache wheel downloads for Poetry and dependencies.

docs.title: 6.4 Matrix Execution Optimization
docs.text:
The CI matrix covers all active NetBox 4.x minor releases: 

matrix:
  netbox-version: ["v4.0", "v4.1", "v4.2", "v4.5"]
All matrix cells execute in parallel on separate free runners, finishing the entire validation suite in parallel within 3 minutes.

docs.title: 6.5 Canary Cron & Automated Issue Generation
docs.text: The weekly canary cron (schedule: - cron: '0 6 * * 1') acts as an early-warning radar. If upstream NetBox pushes an update that breaks the plugin, maintainers are notified immediately via GitHub issues and workflow failure notifications before any end-users are impacted.

docs.title: 7. Step-by-Step Minor Upgrade Procedure (NetBox 4.x → 4.y)
docs.text:
When upstream NetBox publishes a new minor version (for example, upgrading from 4.2 to 4.3), follow this systematic 5-phase procedure:

[Phase 1: Upstream Reconnaissance]
  ├── Read Upstream Release Notes & Breaking Changes
  └── Identify Model & API Changes in core, dcim, ipam
          │
          ▼
[Phase 2: Local Docker Development & Test Execution]
  ├── Update NETBOX_VER in development/dev.env or Dockerfile
  ├── Run docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py makemigrations --check
  └── Run docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics --keepdb
          │
          ▼
[Phase 3: Migration Dependency Audit]
  ├── If new migrations generated, check dependencies list
  └── Pin upstream dependencies to lowest viable migration (e.g. core.0008)
          │
          ▼
[Phase 4: CI Matrix & Configuration Update]
  ├── Add new minor version (v4.y) to .github/workflows/ci.yml matrix
  └── Verify 100% green build on GitHub Actions
          │
          ▼
[Phase 5: Version Bump, Changelog & Release]
  ├── Bump version in pyproject.toml and netbox_more_metrics/__init__.py
  ├── Update docs/changelog.md
  └── Tag release (e.g. v0.4.2) and push

docs.title: Phase 1: Pre-Upgrade Upstream Reconnaissance
docs.text:
1. Read the upstream NetBox release notes for v4.y.0.
  2. Inspect the "Breaking Changes" and "Deprecations" sections.
  3. Check if any core models used in metric filters (e.g., Device, Site, Prefix, VirtualMachine) have renamed fields or altered relational foreign keys.

docs.title: Phase 2: Local Docker Development & Test Execution
docs.text:
1. Update NETBOX_VER to test against the new version: 
    NETBOX_VER=v4.y docker compose build netbox
  2. Start test dependencies and verify migration status: 
    NETBOX_VER=v4.y docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py makemigrations --check
  3. Execute the full automated test suite: 
    NETBOX_VER=v4.y docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics --keepdb
  4. If any tests fail, address the specific API changes following minimal-change and backward-compatible principles.

docs.title: Phase 3: Migration Dependency Audit & makemigrations Verification
docs.text:
1. If any new migrations were created during the update: 
    ls -la netbox_more_metrics/migrations/
  2. Inspect the latest migration file.
  3. Verify that any dependency on core is pinned to the earliest viable migration (core.0008_contenttype_proxy or core.0010_gfk_indexes) rather than the leaf migration of v4.y.
  4. Re-run makemigrations --check to ensure no lingering schema drifts.

docs.title: Phase 4: CI Matrix Update & Verification
docs.text:
1. Open .github/workflows/ci.yml.
  2. Add v4.y to the test job matrix: 
    matrix:
  netbox-version: ["v4.0", "v4.1", "v4.2", "v4.5", "v4.y"]
  3. Commit to the working branch and push to trigger CI.
  4. Verify that all packaging and test matrix cells pass with 100% success.

docs.title: Phase 5: Version Bump, Changelog, and Release Tagging
docs.text:
1. Update version number in pyproject.toml and netbox_more_metrics/__init__.py.
  2. Add release highlights to docs/changelog.md.
  3. Create and push a signed Git tag: 
    git tag -s v0.4.2 -m "Release v0.4.2: NetBox 4.y compatibility"
git push origin v0.4.2

docs.title: 8. Step-by-Step Major Upgrade Playbook (NetBox 4.x → 5.x)
docs.text: Major upgrades introduce fundamental architectural shifts (such as Python version deprecations, Django major upgrades, or plugin API restructuring).

docs.title: Phase 1: Breaking Changes & Deprecation Removal Audit
docs.text:
1. Audit all deprecations removed in NetBox 5.0.
  2. Check whether Django has removed previously deprecated queryset methods or template tags.
  3. Identify whether NetBox 5.0 has introduced a new plugin base class, navigation menu system, or authentication pipeline.

docs.title: Phase 2: Platform Version Bumps (Python, Django, Poetry dependencies)
docs.text:
1. Verify minimum Python runtime. If NetBox 5.0 drops Python 3.10 and requires Python 3.12+, update pyproject.toml: 
    requires-python = ">=3.12"
  2. Update Poetry lockfile: 
    poetry update

docs.title: Phase 3: Core Framework Shims & Model Traversal Adaptations
docs.text:
1. If NetBox 5.0 introduces breaking changes to NetBoxModel or NetBoxModelFilterSet, create backward-compatible adapter shims: 
    try:
    from netbox.filtersets import NetBoxModelFilterSet
except ImportError:
    # Fallback or shim for evolving framework classes
    ...
  2. Verify that validate_field_path() continues to correctly resolve fields across modified models.

docs.title: Phase 4: Migration Path & Data Transformation
docs.text:
1. Ensure the migration path from 4.x to 5.x is linear and non-destructive.
  2. If major schema refactoring is required, generate squashed migrations for old releases or maintain a clean transition migration.
  3. Test migration rollback and re-application against live PostgreSQL test databases.

docs.title: Phase 5: PluginConfig Boundary Update & E2E Validation
docs.text:
1. Update NetBoxMoreMetricsConfig in netbox_more_metrics/__init__.py: 
    min_version = "4.0.0"
max_version = "5.99.9"
  2. Update .github/workflows/ci.yml matrix to include NetBox 5.0 images.
  3. Run complete adversarial stress testing across all metrics collectors and export endpoints.

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting, Rollback, and Emergency Response Runbook
9.1 Scrape 500 Internal Server Errors & Scrape Timeout Remediation
docs.text:
• Symptom: Prometheus server alerts with ScrapeFailed or HTTP 500 status when scraping /plugins/more-metrics/export/.
  • Diagnosis:
  • Inspect the NetBox container logs: 
    docker compose logs --tail=100 netbox
  • Identify the specific metric causing the failure:
    • Scrape metrics individually via the single-metric endpoint: http://netbox:8000/api/plugins/more-metrics/metrics/<pk>/metrics/
    • Iterate across all configured metrics to pinpoint the failing primary key.
  • Immediate Mitigation:
  • Log in to the NetBox admin UI (/plugins/more-metrics/metrics/).
  • Locate the failing metric record and toggle enabled = False.
  • Scrapes will immediately recover.
  • Root-Cause Fix: If the failure was caused by an upstream model change (e.g., a field was renamed or a method return type changed), update collectors.py with defensive try/except containment and deploy a patch release.

docs.title: 9.2 Migration Conflict / NodeNotFoundError Invalidation & Resolution
docs.text:
• Symptom: During manage.py migrate, NetBox crashes with: NodeNotFoundError: Migration netbox_more_metrics.000X dependencies reference nonexistent parent node ('core', '...').
  • Diagnosis: A plugin migration file was generated in an environment running a newer NetBox version, capturing a leaf migration that does not exist in the user's NetBox installation.
  • Remediation:
  • Open the offending migration file in netbox_more_metrics/migrations/.
  • Locate the invalid dependency (e.g., ('core', '0021_job_queue_name')).
  • Replace it with the base dependency present in all 4.x versions: ('core', '0008_contenttype_proxy').
  • Save and re-run: 
    python manage.py migrate netbox_more_metrics

docs.title: 9.3 Registry Collision & Duplicate Timeseries Triage
docs.text:
• Symptom: Scrape endpoint returns Prometheus formatting error: Duplicated timeseries in CollectorRegistry: ....
  • Diagnosis: Two separate metrics within the same collection share the same metric_name and produce identical label sets, or a utilization metric was queried without unique identifying labels.
  • Remediation:
  • The plugin automatically deduplicates utilization samples in DynamicMetricCollector._collect_utilization().
  • If custom user labels collide, adjust the metric_labels configuration to include distinguishing attributes (e.g., id, name, or slug).

docs.title: 9.4 Emergency Patching & Rollback Workflow
docs.text:
If a critical defect is identified in a published release: 1. Branch from Release Tag: 

git checkout -b hotfix/v0.4.2 v0.4.1
2. Apply Minimal Fix: Follow the minimal-change principle. Fix only the defect. 3. Run Regression Tests: 
docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics --keepdb
4. Publish Hotfix: Tag and publish v0.4.2 immediately. 5. Merge Back to Development: Merge hotfix/v0.4.2 into development.

docs.title: Appendix A: Diagnostic Commands Quick Reference
docs.text: Action Executable Command Validate Packaging poetry check Build Artifacts poetry build Check Migrations docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py makemigrations --check Run All Tests docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics --keepdb Run Specific Test docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics.tests.test_collectors --keepdb Test With Warnings docker compose run --rm netbox python -W error::DeprecationWarning ./manage.py test netbox_more_metrics --keepdb Inspect DB Migrations docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py showmigrations Rollback Migration docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py migrate netbox_more_metrics 0007 Re-apply Migrations docker compose run --rm netbox ./manage.py migrate netbox_more_metrics Validate Workflow YAML python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"

docs.title: Appendix B: Migration Dependency Inspection Cheat Sheet
docs.text:
NetBox Core App Migration Flow:
core.0001_squashed_0005
     │
     ▼
core.0008_contenttype_proxy   <--- PIN HERE for core.ObjectType dependencies!
     │                             (Guaranteed to exist across ALL NetBox 4.x)
     ▼
core.0010_gfk_indexes
     │
     ▼
core.0018_concrete_objecttype
     │
     ▼
core.0021_job_queue_name      <--- DO NOT PIN HERE!
                                   (Only exists in NetBox 4.5+; breaks 4.0-4.4)

Rule of Thumb: When referencing any NetBox core model in plugin migrations, never rely on auto-generated leaf migrations. Always pin to the earliest migration that introduced the model definition.
